examples.en: I knead the dough by hand for a long time.

examples.ko: 빵을 만들 때 반죽을 힘껏 치댔어요.
examples.en: When making bread, I kneaded the dough with all my strength.

examples.ko: 쫄깃한 수제비를 만들려면 반죽을 많이 치대야 해요.
examples.en: To make chewy sujebi, you have to knead the dough a lot.
I knead the clay to make it soft.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마한테 치대며 놀아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: The child clings to Mom, asking her to play.

examples.ko: 동생이 자꾸 치대서 숙제를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling kept pestering me, so I couldn't do my homework.

explain: '주무르다'보다 손바닥이나 팔에 힘을 주어 눌러 가며 문지르는 느낌이에요. 빵, 수제비, 칼국수 반죽을 만들 때 많이 써요. 또 사람에게 자꾸 달라붙어 귀찮게 구는 모습에도 쓰는데, 이때는 편한 사이의 대화에서 써요.

phrases.en: If you knead the sujebi dough well, it becomes chewy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반죽을 힘주어 누르며 문지를 때 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical collocation for pressing and working dough with force.

phrases.example: 동생이 자꾸 치대서 숙제를 못 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling keeps clinging to me, so I can't do my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 달라붙어 귀찮게 구는 뜻으로 편한 사이에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to cling and pester someone; used casually among close people.

phrases.en: Please work the dough with your hands.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치대다'보다 힘을 덜 주고 부드럽게 만지는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels gentler than 'chidaeda', using less force.

explain_en: Compared with '주무르다', it has the feel of pressing and rubbing with the palm or arm putting in some force. It is often used for making dough for bread, sujebi and kalguksu. It is also used for someone who keeps clinging to and bothering a person, and in that sense it is for casual conversation.

t90.ax: I knead the clay to make it soft.

en: to eat only what one wants

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 채소를 안 먹고 편식해요.
examples.en: My child doesn't eat vegetables and is a picky eater.

examples.ko: 편식하면 키가 안 클 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you're a picky eater, you may not grow tall.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 편식했는데 지금은 다 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: I was a picky eater as a child, but now I eat everything.
I'm trying to fix my habit of picky eating.

examples.ko: 급식 시간에 아이들이 편식하지 않도록 선생님이 도와줘요.
examples.en: At lunch time, the teacher helps the children not to eat only what they like.
After being a picky eater for a long time, my body got weaker.

explain: 좋아하는 음식만 먹고 다른 음식은 안 먹는 습관이에요. 아이에게는 '편식하지 마'라고 자주 말하고, 같은 뜻의 '가리다'는 '음식을 가리다'로 써요. 반대로 뭐든 잘 먹는 사람은 '골고루 먹다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 편식하지 않고 다 잘 먹어요.
phrases.en: I'm not a picky eater and eat everything well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 가리지 않고 먹는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you eat without being picky.
phrases.en_equiv: not to be a picky eater

phrases.en: I'm worried because my child is picky about food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편식하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 편식하다, and common in daily talk.

phrases.en: You should eat a bit of everything, including vegetables.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편식하다'의 반대로, 여러 음식을 다 먹는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 편식하다: eating a variety of foods.

explain_en: 편식하다 describes eating only favorite foods. Parents often say 편식하지 마 to children; the verb 가리다 works in 음식을 가리다 for the same idea. The opposite habit is expressed with 골고루 먹다.

examples.en: A lot of seaweed washed up on the beach.
I like seaweed salad.
The fish are hiding among the seaweed.

examples.ko: 해초를 말려서 차로 마시는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places dry seaweed and drink it as tea.
Seaweed wrapped around my foot and it startled me.
It tastes good because it grew in clean seawater.

explain: 먹는 바다 식물은 보통 '미역', '김', '다시마'처럼 이름을 따로 불러요. 해초는 바다 식물 전체를 묶어서 말할 때 써요. 그래서 식당에서는 '해초 샐러드'처럼 메뉴 이름에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: This restaurant is famous for its seaweed dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해초로 만든 음식을 두루 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for any food made from sea plants.

phrases.en: People in Japan often eat seaweed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 대상으로 말할 때 '해초를'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '해초를' when it is the thing being eaten.

phrases.en: Haecho are plants that grow in the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해초'를 쉬운 말로 풀어서 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain way to explain what '해초' means.

explain_en: Edible sea plants usually go by their own names such as '미역', '김' and '다시마'. 해초 groups all of them together. You often see it in menu names like '해초 샐러드'.

en: flavor enhancer; artificial flavors; chemical condiment

examples.ko: 이 식당은 화학조미료를 안 쓴다고 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: This restaurant says it doesn't use artificial flavor enhancers.

examples.ko: 어머니는 화학조미료 대신 멸치 육수를 쓰세요.
examples.en: My mother uses anchovy broth instead of chemical seasoning.
I want to avoid food with chemical seasoning in it.

examples.ko: 라면 스프에 화학조미료가 들어 있는지 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked whether the ramen seasoning packet contains artificial flavoring.
These days there are many products with no added chemical seasoning.

examples.ko: 화학조미료를 많이 넣은 국은 맛이 너무 진해요.
examples.en: Soup with a lot of chemical seasoning tastes too strong.

explain: 음식 이야기에서는 그냥 '조미료'라고도 많이 말해요. '무첨가', '안 쓴다'와 같이 쓰이는 경우가 많고, 반대쪽 느낌의 말은 '천연 조미료'예요.

phrases.en: I put only a little seasoning in this soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '화학조미료'를 줄여 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, 'hwahakjomiryo' is often shortened to this.

phrases.example: 저는 멸치로 만든 천연 조미료를 써요.
phrases.en: I use a natural seasoning made from anchovies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화학조미료와 반대되는 느낌의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite feel of chemical seasoning.

phrases.en: I heard that restaurant doesn't add chemical seasoning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넣다/안 넣다'는 음식 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Add / not add' is a common pair in food talk.

explain_en: In food talk, people often just say '조미료'. It often appears with '무첨가' or '안 쓴다', and the opposite idea is '천연 조미료' (natural seasoning).

examples.ko: 기차 맨 앞에서 기관차가 열차를 끌어요.
examples.en: At the front of the train, the locomotive pulls the cars.
I saw an old steam locomotive at the museum.

examples.ko: 기관차는 열차 맨 앞에 달려 있어요.
examples.en: The locomotive is attached at the very front of the train.
My child likes the toy locomotive best.
I heard the sound of a locomotive from far away.

examples.ko: 새 기관차로 바꾼 지 얼마 안 됐어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been long since they changed to a new locomotive.

explain: 열차를 끌고 가는 맨 앞 차량이 '기관차'이고, 사람이 타는 칸은 '객차', 짐을 싣는 칸은 '화물차'라고 해요. 평소에는 전체를 그냥 '기차'라고 부르는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 증기 기관차를 타 봤어요.
phrases.en: I rode a steam locomotive when I was little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 석탄으로 움직이는 옛날 기관차를 말해요. 박물관이나 관광 열차에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An old locomotive that runs on coal, often heard at museums or tourist trains.

phrases.en: There are many electric locomotives these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전기로 가는 기관차예요. '증기 기관차'와 비교해서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A locomotive powered by electricity; handy for comparing with the steam type.

phrases.en: They connected the locomotive and the passenger cars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끄는 차량과 사람이 타는 칸을 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when naming the pulling car and the passenger cars together.

explain_en: The front car that pulls the train is the 기관차, the cars people ride in are 객차, and the cars carrying freight are 화물차. In daily talk people usually call the whole thing just '기차'.

examples.en: At the folk village I tried traditional games with the kids.

examples.ko: 민속촌에서는 옛 풍속을 직접 체험해 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At the folk village you can experience old customs firsthand.
Many foreign tourists visit the folk village.
Do you want to go to the folk village this weekend?
The folk village is a nice place to look around in hanbok.
I also ate traditional food inside the folk village.

explain: 옛날 집과 생활 모습을 보여 주는 관광지를 가리켜요. 특정 장소 이름으로 '한국민속촌'을 줄여 말할 때도 있지만, 일반 명사로도 써요.

phrases.en: I'm going to the folk village with my family this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나들이 계획을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for talking about an outing plan.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the folk village

phrases.en: The trip to the folk village was really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 다녀온 여행이나 소풍 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of a light day trip or outing.
phrases.en_equiv: a trip to the folk village

phrases.en: I went to the Korean Folk Village with a foreign friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정 장소의 이름으로 쓸 때는 '한국민속촌'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '한국민속촌' when naming that specific place.

explain_en: It refers to a tourist site that shows old houses and the way people used to live. People also use it as a short name for 한국민속촌 (the Korean Folk Village), but it works as a common noun too.

examples.ko: 길 반대편에 작은 약국이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small pharmacy on the opposite side of the street.
To take the subway, please go to the opposite platform.
I sat on the chair opposite the window.
You have to take the bus from the other side.
Yesterday I walked all the way to the other side of the lake.
In the debate, my friend and I took opposite sides.

explain: '건너편'은 길이나 강처럼 건너야 하는 곳의 맞은쪽이고, 반대편은 건너지 않아도 '이쪽이 아닌 쪽'이면 써요. 지하철 승강장은 '반대편 승강장'이라고 해요. 장소뿐 아니라 팀이나 의견처럼 서로 맞서는 쪽에도 써요.

phrases.en: There is a cafe on the other side of the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반대편'과 비슷하지만 길이나 강을 건너야 하는 맞은쪽일 때만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but only for the side across a road or river.

phrases.en: I'm waiting on the opposite platform.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지하철에서 가는 방향이 다른 승강장을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in the subway for the platform going the other direction.

phrases.en: Please go to the opposite side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 반대쪽으로 움직인다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 으로 it means moving toward the opposite side.

explain_en: '건너편' is the far side of something you cross, like a road or river, while 반대편 is simply 'the side that is not this one', with no crossing needed. A subway platform is called '반대편 승강장'. It also works for opposing teams or opinions, not only places.

t90.ax: I sat on the chair opposite the window.

en: to cut across; to take a shortcut

examples.en: My friend suggested taking a shortcut through the back alley.
We are late, so let's cut through the park.
I tried to take a shortcut and got lost.

examples.ko: 질러가는 길은 좁지만 십 분이나 빨라요.
examples.en: The shortcut is narrow, but it is ten minutes faster.
It was raining, so I cut through the underpass.
If you are in a hurry, cut through that alley over there.

explain: 큰길로 돌지 않고 더 가까운 길로 곧장 가는 것이라서 '지름길로 가다'와 비슷해요. 반대는 '돌아가다'예요. '공원을 질러가다'처럼 '~을/를 질러가다'나 '~(으)로 질러가다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 지름길로 가면 십 분 일찍 도착해요.
phrases.en: If you take the shortcut, you'll arrive ten minutes earlier.
phrases.nuance_ko: '질러가다'와 비슷하지만 '지름길'이라는 가까운 길을 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is similar to '질러가다' but names the shortcut road clearly.

phrases.en: This is the shortcut route to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 길을 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form modifies the word 'road'.

phrases.en: If you cut through the alley, you'll arrive sooner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 '을/를'로 받아 그곳을 가로질러 간다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place takes '을/를' to say you cut across it.

explain_en: It means going straight by a closer way instead of taking the long main road, so it is close to '지름길로 가다'. The opposite is '돌아가다'. You say '공원을 질러가다' or '골목으로 질러가다'.

examples.en: The marathon starting point is in front of City Hall.
The starting point of this trip is Seoul Station.

examples.ko: 우리 모두 출발점에서 열 시에 만나요.
examples.en: Let's all meet at the starting point at ten.

examples.ko: 한 바퀴를 걷고 출발점으로 다시 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I walked one lap and came back to the starting point.

examples.ko: 등산 출발점까지 버스로 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes by bus to the hiking starting point.

examples.ko: 이 길은 올레길 일 코스의 출발점이에요.
examples.en: This path is the starting point of Olle Trail Course 1.

explain: 같은 자리를 '시작점'이라고도 하지만 길이나 경기 이야기에서는 출발점이 더 자연스러워요. 달리기처럼 땅에 그은 선은 '출발선'이라고 해서 더 구체적이에요. 반대말은 '도착점'이에요.

phrases.en: This is the starting point of the walking trail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출발점'과 비슷하지만 길보다 일 전반에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but it can also apply to things other than roads.

phrases.en: The runners stood at the starting line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달리기처럼 땅에 그은 선을 말해서 더 구체적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More specific, a line drawn on the ground like in a race.

phrases.en: The finish point is the park entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '출발점'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 출발점.

explain_en: The same spot can be called '시작점' too, but for roads and races 출발점 sounds more natural. The line drawn on the ground for a race is '출발선', which is more specific. The opposite is '도착점' (finish point).

t90.ax: Let's all meet at the starting point at ten.

examples.en: I practice alone while looking at a piano manual.
This guitar manual suits beginners well.

examples.ko: 서점에서 요리 교본을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a cooking guidebook at the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이 책은 운전 교본처럼 설명이 쉬워요.
examples.en: This book explains things easily, like a driving manual.

examples.ko: 교본대로 따라 했는데도 잘 안 됐어요.
examples.en: I followed the manual exactly, but it did not work.
The teacher teaches with a manual they wrote themselves.

explain: 학교 교과서보다는 악기, 운동, 요리처럼 기술을 처음 배우는 책에 써요. 학교 수업에서는 '교과서'라고 하고, 교본은 '기본을 익히는 책'에 가까워요. 비유로 '모범'이라는 뜻으로 '교본 같은 사람'이라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I tried cooking by following a cooking manual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기술 이름 뒤에 붙여 어떤 기술을 배우는 책인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put after a skill name to say what the book teaches.

phrases.en: I learned drawing by myself with a manual.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선생님 없이 책으로 익힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when learning from a book without a teacher.

phrases.en: Please open your math textbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 수업에서 쓰는 책이에요. '교본'과 구분해서 알아 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: The book used in school classes; distinguish it from 교본.

explain_en: Rather than a school textbook, it is used for books that teach a skill from the start, such as an instrument, sport or cooking. In school lessons Koreans say 교과서. Figuratively, 교본 같은 사람 can describe a person who is a perfect model.

en: school record (grades counted for college admission)

examples.ko: 내신 성적이 좋아야 원하는 대학에 가요.
examples.en: You need good school record grades to get into the college you want.

examples.ko: 시험이 내신에 반영된다고 해서 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: I worked hard because the exam counts toward my school record.
Because of school record grades, my friends study even during vacation.
I changed cram schools to raise my school record grade.
I'm more worried about my school record than the CSAT.

examples.ko: 내신 시험이 다음 주라서 도서관에 갔어요.
examples.en: My school exam is next week, so I went to the library.

explain: 대학 입시 이야기에서 나오는 말이에요. 학교 안에서 받은 성적이 내신이고, 한 번에 보는 '수능'과 구분해요. 학교 시험 점수 자체는 그냥 '성적'이라고 해요. '내신이 좋다/나쁘다', '내신 등급'으로 말해요.

phrases.en: My school record grade went up, so I'm happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 성적을 등급으로 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing used when talking about school grades as ranked levels.

phrases.en: My school record is good, so I got a strong recommendation too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내신'을 평가할 때 '좋다/나쁘다'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'good/bad' to evaluate someone's school record.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a good school record

phrases.en: Managing your school record is important for high school students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험과 수행평가로 학교 성적을 챙기는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to keeping your in-school grades on track through exams and assignments.

explain_en: This word comes up when talking about college admission. Grades earned inside school are 내신, set apart from the one-time 수능 exam. A school test score by itself is simply 성적. It is used as 내신이 좋다/나쁘다 and 내신 등급.

examples.en: I ignored my homework and only played games.
You can't abandon your responsibility and run away.
The child flung their bag down in the entryway and left it.
Word got around that he's someone who abandoned his family.
They do half the work and then just drop it.
Don't blow off your promise to a friend.

explain: 물건을 홱 던져 버린다는 뜻도 있지만, 일, 책임, 사람을 돌보지 않고 저버릴 때 더 많이 써요. 물리적으로 거칠게 던지는 동작은 '내동댕이치다'가 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: He abandoned his family and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내팽개치다'보다 조금 짧고 뜻은 거의 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly shorter form with almost the same meaning as '내팽개치다'.

phrases.example: 일을 내팽개치고 놀러 가면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not drop your work and go out to play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일을 책임지지 않고 버려 둘 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for abandoning work you should be doing.

phrases.en: Even if it's hard, don't give up on your studies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 말리거나 당부할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to advise or urge someone not to do it.

explain_en: It can mean flinging something away, but it is used more for abandoning work, responsibility or people without caring for them. For a rough physical throw, '내동댕이치다' fits better.

examples.en: My rank went up a lot on this exam.
My rank is tenth in the class.
I decided not to compare ranks with my friend.

examples.ko: 등수에 너무 신경 쓰면 공부가 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you worry too much about rank, studying gets hard.

examples.ko: 달리기 시합에서 등수 안에 들지 못했어요.
examples.en: I didn't place in the running race.

examples.ko: 선생님이 등수 대신 점수만 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us only our scores instead of ranks.

explain: '몇 등이냐'를 말할 때의 그 숫자를 가리켜요. 시험, 달리기, 대회 순위에 두루 쓰고, 학교 성적 순위는 '석차'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 공부를 안 했더니 등수가 많이 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: I didn't study, so my rank dropped a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순위가 낮아졌다는 뜻이고, 반대는 '등수가 오르다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the rank went down; the opposite is 등수가 오르다.

phrases.en: The teacher ranked us by our running times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기록이나 점수를 보고 순서를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for deciding order based on records or scores.

phrases.en: What place did you get in this contest?
phrases.nuance_ko: 순위를 물을 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest way to ask about someone's ranking.

explain_en: It refers to the number in 'what place did you get'. It works for exams, races and contests, and a school grade ranking is also called '석차'.

t90.ax: My rank is tenth in the class.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 오월 말에 모내기를 해요.
examples.en: This village transplants rice seedlings at the end of May.
Once the rice planting is done, the paddies turn green.

examples.ko: 비가 알맞게 와서 올해는 물 걱정 없이 모내기를 마쳤어요.
examples.en: The rain came at just the right time, so this year we finished rice planting without worrying about water.
Many hands are needed during the rice-planting season.
During rice planting, neighbors help one another.
These days they plant rice seedlings by machine, so it is much faster.

explain: 볍씨를 키운 모를 논에 옮겨 심는 일이에요. 보통 늦봄에서 초여름에 하고, 그때를 '모내기철'이라고 해요. 동사 '모내다'보다 '모내기를 하다'처럼 명사로 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 비가 온 뒤에 마을 사람들이 모내기를 했어요.
phrases.en: The villagers planted rice seedlings after the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 일을 말할 때 가장 기본이 되는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to talk about this work.

phrases.en: During rice-planting season the countryside is very busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모내기를 하는 늦봄에서 초여름을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to late spring to early summer, when rice is planted.

phrases.example: 모내기가 끝나서 이제 좀 쉴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Rice planting is done, so we can rest a little now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝났음을 말할 때 주어로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as the subject when the work is finished.

explain_en: It is the work of moving young rice seedlings into the paddy. It usually happens from late spring to early summer, and that period is called '모내기철'. People more often use the noun, as in '모내기를 하다', than the verb '모내다'.

t90.ax: During rice planting, neighbors help one another.
